source_note: PLACEHOLDER mastery/readiness weights. Every number is invented to make the engine runnable and MUST be checked against pedagogy/product intent before it is trusted (see docs/TO_VERIFY.md).

source_weights.why: PLACEHOLDER: teacher grades are the most trusted signal, quizzes next, self-directed flashcards least; a source the student chooses freely should not outweigh a graded assessment.

difficulty_weights.why: PLACEHOLDER: solving a harder question is stronger evidence of mastery than an easy one; the scale is deliberately mild so one hard question cannot dominate many easy ones.

half_life_days_why: PLACEHOLDER: memory evidence loses half its weight in about a month; recency matters but old evidence should still count a little.

per_question_repeat_cap.why: PLACEHOLDER: answering the same question many times in a week is one observation, not many; cap the total weight from one question inside the window so drilling a single item cannot fake mastery.

confidence.why: PLACEHOLDER: a mastery number needs enough effective evidence spread over more than one day; below the minimum the result is NONE, and below the low fraction (of the minimum) it is LOW.

readiness.why: PLACEHOLDER: a chapter/subject readiness is only reported when at least half of its topics carry evidence; below that the sample is too sparse to mean anything.

readiness_bands.why: PLACEHOLDER: band boundaries (<0.4 WEAK, <0.6 DEVELOPING, <0.8 SECURE, else STRONG) chosen to read as needs-work / progressing / solid / mastered.

trend.why: PLACEHOLDER: compare evidence in the last two weeks against the earlier window and only call UP/DOWN when mastery moved by more than the threshold; otherwise FLAT, and UNKNOWN when there is too little recent evidence.
